report:
## Research Findings: Does a Vegetarian Diet Increase Life Expectancy?

The evidence is more mixed and nuanced than the claim suggests.

**Cause-specific benefits, but not clear all-cause mortality reduction:** A 2021 meta-analysis found vegetarian diets were associated with reduced ischemic heart disease mortality, but had **no significant effect on all-cause mortality**, and the authors cautioned that certainty of evidence was low (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34611632/). Similarly, large British cohort studies (EPIC-Oxford, Health Food Shoppers Study, Oxford Vegetarian Study) found **almost identical all-cause mortality** between vegetarians and non-vegetarians, with EPIC-Oxford even showing slightly (non-significantly) *higher* mortality in vegetarians (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002916522033536).

**Some supportive meta-analyses exist:** More recent 2025 meta-analyses of plant-based diet indices report an association between healthful plant-based eating patterns and reduced mortality (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2025.1518519/full), though these examine "plant-based diet scores" rather than strict vegetarianism, and observational designs can't establish causation.

**Contradictory findings on extreme longevity:** A large study of centenarians in China found vegetarians (including vegans) were **less likely to reach age 100** than meat-eaters, though those who included fish, dairy, or eggs did as well as meat-eaters — suggesting overall dietary balance/nutritional adequacy matters more than avoiding meat per se (https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018122).

**A 2025 review concludes it's complicated:** "Vegetarian diets for longevity: friend or foe?" highlights that while vegetarians tend to have lower rates of certain chronic diseases, questions remain about nutrient adequacy (e.g., fracture risk) that could offset longevity gains (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378512225005195).

**Conclusion:** The claim is **not well-supported as stated**. Evidence suggests vegetarian diets may reduce risk of specific diseases (like heart disease) but show inconsistent or null effects on overall life expectancy, and some studies suggest well-planned diets including some animal products may support longevity as well as or better than strict vegetarianism.
